explanation:
[EFFECT]
Humidity has a non-monotonic but broadly declining effect on predicted bike demand. At low-to-moderate humidity levels (roughly 10%–40%, i.e. about 10–40%), the contribution is slightly positive and fairly flat, with a small peak around 36% humidity. Beyond that point, the contribution falls steadily, crossing into negative territory around 70% humidity, and reaching its lowest values near 100% humidity — where predicted demand is roughly 23% lower than the model's baseline. (The very lowest humidity point, near 2%, shows an unusually negative contribution, but this likely reflects very rare conditions with few observations.)

[IMPORTANCE]
Humidity ranks 5th out of 9 features in terms of importance (importance score: 0.083), making it a mid-level driver of demand. It matters, but hour of the day, temperature, and year have a stronger influence on predictions.

[RECOMMENDATION]
When high humidity is forecast (above roughly 70%), expect noticeably lower ridership — consider reducing bike redistribution efforts and staff hours during those periods, as demand is unlikely to be strong regardless of other conditions.
